solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Altered borders ultimately all will be disputed

indicators.note: as a verb, to border something is to run along its edges, so CHANGED sits on both sides of the other letters
ultimately means at the end, so each word gives up its final letter

blocks.note: last letters of alL, wilL, bE

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the borders were redrawn and every one of them will now be contested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Borders' looks like a noun about frontiers; here it is a verb, CHANGED going around the other letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a result or claim that someone has contested has been called into question.

clue.text: I approve this location for those attending more than once

indicators.note: to attend can mean to listen, so those attending are the listeners, and the word is given as they receive it
the phrase is to be said again, so the same sound appears twice in a row

explanation.surface: A note about a venue that suits people who come back repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: HEAR HEAR is what members of the British Parliament call out to back a speaker. 'Those attending' sounds like visitors, but it means listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the cry is a spoken show of agreement from an audience, standing for the speaker's own 'I approve'.

clue.text: Pound sheltering a dog

indicators.note: to shelter something is to keep it inside, so the pound symbol keeps A within it

blocks.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: A dogs' home takes in a stray.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pound is an animal shelter; the wordplay wants the weight, LB. The A inside the pound does double duty in the definition 'a dog'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this is the everyday short name for the Labrador retriever, one breed of dog.

clue.text: Guard at gate failing to open gate, perhaps

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, and failing to have it means that letter goes

blocks.note: a soldier posted on guard; lose its first letter
surface padding: says where the guard stands

explanation.surface: A gatekeeper cannot get the gate to open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing to open' reads as a stuck gate, but it tells you to remove the S from SENTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a gate is one kind of way in, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Book group?

blocks.note: the first book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A book club, or someone asking for a book group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book group' sounds like a reading circle; split it and each word is its own definition of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the opening book of the Old Testament, and the rock band of Phil Collins and Peter Gabriel.

clue.text: In France, some bother nabbing a reckless criminal

indicators.note: the word wanted is the one a French speaker would use for 'some'
to nab is to grab, so the bother takes hold of the next piece and keeps it right against itself

blocks.note: a = per, as in ten pounds a head

explanation.surface: A French police report: a spot of trouble ends in the arrest of a dangerous outlaw.
explanation.walkthrough: The easy thing to miss is A = PER, from prices like 'two pounds a kilo'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from Spanish, familiar from Westerns: a bold, violent outlaw with nothing to lose.

clue.text: Some people have returned to lend a hand

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the words are used
to return is to go back the way you came, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: the last three letters of 'people' and the first of 'have'

explanation.surface: Some people have come back to pitch in.
explanation.walkthrough: The run of letters spans the gap between two words, which is where hidden answers usually sit.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: lending a hand is the everyday phrase for assisting someone.

clue.text: Odd demand shown for used gear

indicators.note: odd means strange, and a strange arrangement of the letters is what is wanted

explanation.surface: A strange request has been made for second-hand equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' looks like it might mean odd letters, but the count shows DEMAND SHOWN is exactly the 11 letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: clothes or kit passed down from an older sibling or earlier owner, so already used.

clue.text: Reduced stuff written on some dull list

indicators.note: reduced means cut down, so the word is shortened to its usual abbreviation
in a down answer, one piece written on another sits above it

blocks.note: stuff written = literature, shortened to LIT

explanation.surface: Cut-down notes jotted onto a boring list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduced' reads as describing a shortened list; it belongs to 'stuff written', trimming literature to LIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: originally a church prayer of repeated petitions, now any long, tedious recital, as in a litany of complaints.

clue.text: Talk continuously, except about potentially boring thing taking place

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, as in 'about turn', so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: bar = except; turned round it is RAB
on = happening, as in 'the match is on'

explanation.surface: Someone talks nonstop, except about something dull happening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' wants to mean dull; it means making holes, so the thing is a drill BIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use: in British slang, to rabbit on is to chatter at length without a pause.

clue.text: Private areas in clubs hosted by one who’s big at present time?

indicators.note: a host has guests inside their home, so the clubs letter goes inside the other word

blocks.clueFragment: one who’s big at present time?
blocks.note: the big figure at Christmas, present time

explanation.surface: Exclusive rooms at clubs laid on by a local bigwig of the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present time' reads as 'now', but it means the time of giving presents, so the big figure is SANTA.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in Latin plural form: a sanctum is a private room or retreat, and these are several of them.

clue.text: Particular house in comfortable surroundings

indicators.note: the house abbreviation goes in the other word
the comfortable word surrounds the house, wrapping round it on both sides

blocks.note: ho. is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A particular house set in snug grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Particular' is not describing the house; it is the definition, meaning fussy.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a particular eater or shopper is hard to please and fussy about what they accept.

clue.text: Regular contributors to robust old group currently not working

indicators.note: letters at regular intervals are the ones contributing, so every other letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: a faction is a group within a party

explanation.surface: Stalwart members of a veteran band are not playing at the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regular contributors' sounds like loyal members of the group; it tells you to take regular letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a machine or player sidelined for now by damage or injury is described this way.

clue.text: Angry snitch admitting what the Mafia disaffirm in the end

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so SING lets the other letters inside it
each word gives up the letter at its end

blocks.note: to sing is to inform on others
last letters of whaT thE mafiA disaffirM

explanation.surface: An informer, furious, confesses what the Mob insist is untrue.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has the Mob denying the informer's story; 'in the end' is a mechanical instruction covering four words.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use: in informal British English, someone steaming is furious, as if boiling over.

clue.text: Trained seals swimming somewhere in the Pacific

indicators.note: things swimming move about freely, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: Circus seals take a swim somewhere out in the Pacific Ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trained' looks like the instruction, but it is part of the letters; 'swimming' does the mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Chilean island famous for its giant stone heads lies in the south-east Pacific.

clue.text: Switch behind large stove

blocks.note: a range is a large cooking stove

explanation.surface: A switch placed behind a big cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch' looks like a noun, a light switch by the cooker; it is a verb meaning to swap round.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to switch things around is to put them in a different order.

clue.text: Illegally enter resort breaking lock

indicators.note: something breaking a word splits it open and sits in the gap

blocks.note: a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: A burglar breaks the lock to get into a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface lock is on a door; the wordplay wants a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: going onto land or into a building without the right to be there.

clue.text: Ostentatious, pro-conflict Democrat giving glimpse of what’s to come

explanation.surface: A showy, hawkish American politician hints at what lies ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pro-conflict' reads as one word for hawkish; split at the hyphen, each half gives its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from film and fiction: a scene that jumps ahead in time, showing the future.

clue.text: Important suspect picked up somewhere secret

indicators.note: picked up by the ear, as a radio picks up a signal

explanation.surface: A leading suspect is arrested at a secret location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' and 'picked up' read as police work; suspect is a verb, and 'picked up' means heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a concealed place where fugitives lie low.

clue.text: Where animals may eat, close to verdant part of golf course

indicators.note: a close is an end, so the end letter of the next word is wanted

blocks.note: the rough is the long grass beside the fairway

explanation.surface: Grazing animals feed beside the green part of a golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' reads as 'near'; it means the end of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the long open container that farm animals feed or drink from.

clue.text: Got reminder to take medicine?

indicators.note: to take something is to hold it, so the reminder holds the medicine inside it

blocks.note: a prod is a nudge or reminder
a cure is one kind of medicine, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Someone received a reminder to take their pills.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a pill alarm; the wordplay makes 'take' mean hold inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, slightly formal: obtained or acquired something, often with some effort.

clue.text: Stop initially doing everything slowly — it’s so thoughtless

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each word gives its first letter

blocks.clueFragment: doing everything slowly — it’s so thoughtless
blocks.note: first letters of Doing Everything Slowly It's So Thoughtless

explanation.surface: A plea to someone to stop dawdling over everything, which is so inconsiderate.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a complete complaint, so the six initials are easy to read past; the dash is only punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as in the legal phrase 'cease and desist': to leave off doing something.

clue.text: Gloomy days are somehow beginning to recede

indicators.note: somehow means in some unstated way, so ARE comes out in some other order
the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Grey days are starting to lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Days' is not part of the definition; it supplies only its abbreviation D.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary use: a poetic, shortened form of dreary, meaning dismal.

clue.text: Possible problem for low-level member of British workers’ collective

explanation.surface: A junior member of a British trade union might be trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low-level member' sounds like a junior union member; it is the foot, the body's lowest limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: a painful swelling at the base of the big toe, trouble for the lowest limb.

clue.text: Clothing company always primarily protected by patent

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the first letter of the word is used
whatever is protected is kept inside, so the letters go within the patent word

explanation.surface: A fashion firm whose designs are always covered by patents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patent' reads as a legal right; here it is the adjective meaning obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a heavy coat worn over other garments is one item of clothing.

clue.text: Vehicle in speed event almost overturned

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word stops one letter short
in a down answer, turned upside down reads backwards

blocks.note: a race, missing its last letter

explanation.surface: A car flipped over during a race.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a crash; 'overturned' is really an instruction to flip the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the motor car is the everyday road vehicle.

clue.text: Weak article reduced in length

indicators.note: a word made shorter loses letters, here just its last one

blocks.note: an article is an object; drop the final G

explanation.surface: A feeble piece of writing has been cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' is not a/an/the here but an object, a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an unconvincing excuse or a watery soup lacks strength.

clue.text: Increase introduced by key power business

indicators.note: whoever introduces something comes before it, so the other pieces lead and RISE follows

blocks.note: the Enter key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: A rise brought in by a leading energy firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key power business' reads as one phrase about an energy company; it breaks into key, power and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a company or commercial venture.
